report.source_text: Subsequent CT angiogram confirmed a pulmonary sling, with the left pulmonary artery arising from the distal right pulmonary artery and wrapping around the distal trachea (Fig. 2). Left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction, consistent with left-sided air trapping, was observed. Moderate-sized patent ductus arteriosus (PDA) and a notable patent foramen ovale (PFO) were present. Furthermore, a right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus) was identified (Fig. 3).

Unfortunately, due to the significant left pulmonary artery hypoplasia she developed recurrent left pulmonary artery stenosis.

clinician.final_diagnosis: left pulmonary arterial sling with an associated right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 6-week-old female presented with respiratory distress, weight loss, and a newly detected murmur. Initial echocardiogram identified left pulmonary arterial sling, prominent patent foramen ovale, and moderate PDA with continuous left to right shunting. Chest CT angiography subsequently confirmed the left pulmonary arterial sling with the left pulmonary artery arising from the right pulmonary artery and encircling the distal trachea, left proximal mainstem bronchus obstruction with air trapping, and identified the associated right upper lobe tracheal bronchus (pig bronchus). At 7 months of age, the patient underwent surgical repair of the left pulmonary artery sling and PDA. Post-operatively, the patient developed left pulmonary artery stenosis, which was treated with balloon angioplasty, but recurrent stenosis occurred due to hypoplasia. Detailed initial physical exam respiratory distress severity and murmur characteristics, postoperative imaging, and later clinical course details were not documented.
